proposals.title: Today's review: one spaced, interleaved, blind queue that never piles up
proposals.what:
A new first tab on /review/: `Today 12 · Redo 25 · Marked 3 · Saved 14 · History 312 · Fixed 40`. Each local day (X-Tz), the server builds a due list from five ladders, all on fresh seeds:
(a) first proofs: mistakes not answered since they opened;
(b) second proofs: mistakes whose first clean answer came on an earlier day (see proposal 2);
(c) check-ins on fixed mistakes (R9: 3, 10 and 30 days);
(d) saved questions on their own ladder of 1, 3, 7, 21 and 60 days, where a clean answer moves up a rung and a miss drops to rung 1 and opens a mistake;
(e) slow-right question types (proposal 5).

Size and order: the cap is 40% of the student's daily minutes (learners.minutes), at least 6 and at most 30 questions. Priority runs relapsed, then confident misses (proposal 4), then overdue, then due. The list is then interleaved so no two questions in a row share a topic. One slot in four is a 'cover' question of new material from progress.coach, so a redo question cannot be spotted as one. No card says 'your mistake' until after Check.

Card at the top of the tab:
- a ring `0 / 12` and the chips `5 first tries · 3 second tries · 2 check-ins · 2 saved`,
- `about 16 min` and the primary **Start today's review**,
- a 7-day forecast strip with a bar and count per day, today highlighted,
- the rule line: 'Each mistake comes back on new numbers until you get it right on two different days.'

When finished: `Done for today · 9 of 12 right · 2 mistakes fixed · 7 due tomorrow`, with the ring full. Unanswered items roll to the top of tomorrow. Anything over the cap waits and is never shown as debt. The nav badge becomes 'due today', not total open. Today's Review card and Plan's Rechecks task read the same list.

What the student does differently: one 15-minute review every day, instead of now and then clearing a 25-row backlog in one sitting. Why it moves the score: spaced retrieval on new numbers, mixed across topics, is the most reliable gain in learning research (spread-out practice beats practice crammed into one sitting, and mixing topics trains choosing the method). Cover questions remove the 'this is the arc one' cue that the real test never gives. A finite daily goal is what keeps a habit going.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has a 'Due Today' list only for vocab words. Their math redo list is always empty (toggleRedo has no button, and Profile reads 'Redo Questions 0'), and 'Solved Only' repeats the same finite items. Our v2 spec spaces only fixed mistakes; the rest is a backlog cleared with 'Redo all · 22'.
proposals.needs:
- GET /api/review/due, plus a pool 'due' in the §2.6 drill body (F5).
- saved gains stage INTEGER and due TEXT (F4).
- traps.proved_at from proposal 2 (F4).
- learners.minutes (R15).
- progress.coach for the cover questions.
- /api/me review.due for the badge (amends R1's open-count badge).
- Today #mist (S3) and Plan Rechecks (S7) read the same endpoint.

proposals.title: Proof that sticks: a mistake closes only on two different days, never right after reading its label
proposals.what:
This changes what closes a trap (R8/R9).
- **Pip 1** can be earned any time, including on the repair question straight after the miss (Repaired).
- **Pip 2** counts only when both hold:
  - it comes on a later local day than pip 1 (traps.proved_at, X-Tz calendar day);
  - it was not answered in the Review pane within 10 minutes of the student viewing that trap's label or rationale. Pane answers of that kind file attempts.primed = 1, fill no second pip, and show 'Practice. The proof comes tomorrow.'

Pip states: ○○ Open → ●○ `Back tomorrow · Sep 24` → ●● Fixed → check-ins at 3, 10 and 30 days (R9).

Other changes:
- drill._pick skips a trap whose proved_at is today.
- The Redo queue asks each template at most once a day, so the header reads `Redo all · 11 questions · about 18 min`, not 22.
- Session feedback copy (S4): 'Right: 1 of 2. It comes back tomorrow on new numbers.'
- The Fixed stat line adds `proved over a median 2 days`.
- Migration: traps closed today stay closed, and their first check-in is due tomorrow.

What the student does differently: they can no longer 'fix' a mistake in five minutes by spotting the trap they just read about. They have to recall the method after some forgetting has set in. Why it moves the score: success in the same session right after feedback measures short-term memory. A right answer after a delay is what predicts test-day performance. It also keeps Fixed honest, so the list reflects what the student will actually get right in March.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's 'Mixed' is wrong-then-right on the same item seconds apart, with unlimited retries. The v2 spec lets a trap close within one session: the repair counts as a clean answer, and practice's _pick asks the topic's open trap again within 3 or 4 questions. In the seeded dev database, all 10 closed traps closed within 30 minutes of opening.
proposals.needs:
- F4: traps.proved_at TEXT, attempts.primed INTEGER, and the progress.record rule change.
- R9's wording amended.
- counts.redo_questions becomes Σ open templates × 1 per day.
- drill._pick change (F5 → S4) and the S4 feedback copy.
- One test_flow assert: two right answers on one day leave owed = 1.

proposals.title: Name your own mistake before we name it, plus an inbox for test misses
proposals.what:
Every new miss enters Redo as `New · not reviewed` (an ink dot). That includes misses from sections, modules and the diagnostic, where no feedback was shown during the test. The tab head reads `6 new misses to look at · about 4 min`, with **Look at new misses**, which steps through them in the pane.

For each miss:
1. The pane shows the question with the student's pick marked and the key hidden.
2. It asks **What happened?** with 4 to 6 choices, shuffled and shown as plain sentences:
   - the misconception behind their pick,
   - the misconceptions behind the item's other wrong options,
   - 'Misread what was asked', 'Arithmetic slip / rushed' and 'Didn't know how to start'.
3. After the tap, the pane reveals the key and the per-option lines, with a verdict: `You called it`, or `Your pick came from: used 180 degrees for a whole circle`.
4. Then **Fresh one like this** (practice only; see proposal 2) and **Next miss**.

Keys: 1–6 to choose, Enter to reveal. The Redo head and the calibration panel show 'You named your own mistake 11 of 17 times (65%)', also per topic. The self-tags that are not misconceptions become Redo filters: Rushed feeds proposal 5, and Didn't know how to start sends the trap to the worked-example step of proposal 6. Grid-ins use spr_mistakes when the template has them (R9), and otherwise only the three general choices.

What the student does differently: they diagnose each error in about 15 seconds instead of glancing at a label, and test misses stop dying unread in a report. Why it moves the score: studies of self-explanation and of studying wrong worked examples (e.g. McLaren et al.) show that students who analyse their errors outperform, on delayed tests, students who were only shown the correction. Being able to name a trap is what lets a student catch it mid-solve on test day.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's 'Distractor Analysis' is passive prose inside one explanation. Their report cannot be re-answered, and their QBank hides the key after a miss. The v2 pane shows the label at once and gives the student nothing to do.
proposals.needs:
- A diagnoses(learner, attempt_id, choice, ok, at) table (F4) and traps.reviewed.
- POST /api/review/diagnose {attempt_id, choice}, which returns the reveal payload through access() 'reveal' (R19).
- A diagnose step in UI.review mode 'pane' (F3).
- spr_mistakes from the QBank bank task.
- A test_flow assert that the key is not returned before the diagnosis is posted.

proposals.title: Confident misses first: calibration across every sitting
proposals.what:
Every answer gets a confidence level:
- 'guess': practice's I'm guessing, or the Tests Guess tag;
- 'unsure': flagged, or the Unsure tag;
- 'sure': the Sure tag, or unflagged and within pace. The inferred case is shown as `sure (assumed)`.

Redo changes:
- Rows get a confidence glyph.
- **Confident misses first** becomes the default sort.
- A stat tile reads `CONFIDENT MISSES 4 · you didn't know you didn't know`.
- A confident miss carries a `Sure ✕` chip until it is fixed, and leads Today's review.

The Marked tab's calibration line becomes a panel:
- a 3×2 grid (Sure / Unsure / Guess × Right / Wrong) with counts and percentages;
- a table per topic;
- rules generated from thresholds: sure-accuracy under 80% in a topic gives 'Linear functions: 5 sure-but-wrong. Check your work here before moving on.' Unsure-accuracy over 70% gives 'Circles: you're right 78% of the time you doubt yourself. Trust your first answer.'

What the student does differently: they work first on the errors they would never have flagged on test day, and learn topic by topic when to trust themselves and when to re-check. Why it moves the score: the hypercorrection effect (Butterfield & Metcalfe) means high-confidence errors, once corrected, are remembered better than low-confidence ones. Unflagged errors never get a second look in Bluebook, so they are pure point loss. A calibrated student spends the last minutes of a module on the right questions.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep counts flags (the red For Review flag, the orange dot) and never relates them to correctness. The v2 spec's calibration is one ratio over flags only, and Tests' calibration is per sitting inside one report.
proposals.needs:
- attempts.guess and attempts.flagged (R8).
- attempts.conf, filled from qstate.conf (R7, S5) and from an optional Sure / Unsure chip in the practice session (S4, behind a pref).
- GET /api/review/calibration → {grid, topics, rules}, computed in SQL.
- The pace targets from proposal 5 for the inferred 'sure'.

proposals.title: Slow but right: the pace list and speed-up sets
proposals.what:
A new Redo kind, `Slow` (clock glyph), computed from data. A template is slow when the student's last 2 right answers on it were both over its tier target, or over twice the student's own median. The tier targets are easy 65s, medium 95s and hard 125s, which gives about 2,090s for a 7/8/7 module against its 2,100s (R34). A row reads `Area of a sector · right 3× · median 2:40 · target 1:35`. Wrong answers given in under 25s get a `Rushed` chip and the rule 'Slow down on these: 4 misses in under 25 s'.

**Speed up** (action bar and pane) builds fresh versions with a target bar on the question strip: it fills orange until the target, then ink, with no hard cutoff. A right answer under target fills a pip, and 2 pips on different days (proposal 2) clear the item.

The History modal and the pane's family strip gain a time sparkline per try with the target line, e.g. `2:40 → 1:52 → 1:21`. A tile reads `SLOW RIGHT 6 · about 9 min over pace per module`.

What the student does differently: they drill the question types that eat their clock, against a visible target, until those types are fast as well as right. Why it moves the score: every minute over pace on a timed module is a question at the end that is rushed, guessed or never reached. Speed on routine types frees time and working memory for the hard ones, and today's mastery bars count slow-right as simply right, which hides the loss.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has a per-question stopwatch that resets on reload and is never analysed; nothing in their product talks about pace. The v2 Review only offers a 'Slowest' sort on History.
proposals.needs:
- attempts.ms in every mode (R7).
- PACE = {easy: 65, medium: 95, hard: 125} in blueprint.py, and one function progress.slow(learner) that Plan's slow-skill rule (S7) also reads.
- Trap kind 'slow' with norm '~slow' (F4).
- Drill cfg target_ms, rendered on the runner strip (F3, S4).

proposals.title: Stuck mistakes get a faded ladder: worked, then hinted, then solo
proposals.what:
A trap missed 3 or more times, or relapsed, gets the status `Stuck`, and its redo becomes a ladder. Each step uses a fresh seed:
1. **Worked.** The question is shown with the key highlighted, the rationale and every option's misconception. The task is 'Tap the option that comes from your mistake', then 'Got it'.
2. **Hinted.** A fresh version with a 'Watch for: used 180 degrees for a whole circle' line above the stem. A right answer fills a hollow step, not a pip, and is filed as attempts.scaffold = 1, which is neither clean nor counted toward mastery.
3. **Solo.** An ordinary fresh question inside Today's review, where a right answer is pip 1.

A miss at any step goes back one step. The pane shows the three steps with the current one ringed. 'Didn't know how to start' from proposal 3 also starts a trap at step 1.

What the student does differently: they stop hammering a question type they keep failing. Instead they study one worked instance, answer one with a hint, then go solo. Why it moves the score: worked-example and fading research (Sweller; Renkl & Atkinson) shows that learners who keep failing gain more from studying worked examples first, and that fading from worked to independent beats problem solving alone. Repeated failure with no new information only repeats the error.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep offers only unlimited retries on the same item, or reading its one explanation. The v2 spec serves another fresh seed of the same trap forever, however many times it is missed.
proposals.needs:
- attempts.scaffold INTEGER, excluded from clean answers and mastery (F4, extends R8).
- traps.stage, 0 to 3.
- Drill cfg scaffold: 'worked' | 'hint' (F5), rendered by UI.workspace (F3).
- Step 1 reuses the Spot-the-trap walk (POST /api/review/spot).

proposals.title: Habits: the handful of mistakes behind dozens of rows
proposals.what:
Redo's Group by gains **Habit** (`Topic | Domain | Mistake type | Habit`). A panel on the Redo head reads, for example: 'Your top habits: Reported the wrong quantity · 9 misses in 6 topics; Halved or doubled · 5 in 3 topics; Sign flip · 4 in 3 topics'.

There are about 10 habits: the wrong quantity asked for, sign, reciprocal or inverse, square vs root, half or double (radius vs diameter included), percent base, added vs multiplied, units, stopped one step early, off by one.

Each habit card has:
- a strip of its misses over time and the topics they came from,
- a one-line test-day check, e.g. 'Before you pick: underline what the question asks for',
- **Drill this habit**: an interleaved set of fresh items across its templates whose options include one of its traps (list 'related', generalised from a norm to a habit).

The mapping lives in server/habits.py: regex rules over the norm, with a bank-side Mis.habit tag overriding them where set. I measured it: over 12 seeds per template there are 2,524 distinct normalised reasons. Crude rules already match 1,187 of them (47%), and 'wrong quantity' alone covers 559 norms across all 19 topics.

What the student does differently: they fix one root habit with one self-check that works in every topic, instead of working through 25 separate labels. Why it moves the score: the same error pattern recurs across topics, and a named general check transfers. Mixing topics trains recognising the habit in a new setting, which is what the SAT demands.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep names no misconceptions at all. The v2 spec's 'same mistake elsewhere' matches only identical normalised text (79 norms), which misses most patterns that cross topics.
proposals.needs:
- server/habits.py: the rules plus an lru_cached index built like progress.related.
- Optional Mis.habit in satbank/item.py (bank owner; this extends the open Mis.tag question).
- Drill pool 'related' accepting {habit} (F5).
- The habit copy is owned here.

proposals.title: Worth most first: rank mistakes by how often they appear on the test
proposals.what:
A new sort, **Worth most**, which is the default on Redo. It ranks by expected questions lost: how often the topic appears on the test, times the student's miss rate on that template's last 5 answers, weighted by tier.
- Topic frequency comes from blueprint: the published 15/15/7/7 domain split per 44 questions, divided among topics by skill counts.
- Group headers show `≈ 4 questions a test`; row meta shows `costs ≈ 0.6 questions a test`.
- The Most-missed strip becomes `Worth most: these 5 cost about 2.4 questions a test → Redo these 5`.
- An optional points line, `≈ +20 points at your level`, uses the slope of the student's current estimate (R16). It is hidden when the estimate's confidence is low.

What the student does differently: with limited time, they fix first the mistakes the real test asks about most. Why it moves the score: a trap in Linear functions (about 4 questions a test) costs more than one in Probability (about 1). Ordering by test frequency times miss rate gives the most points per minute of review.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's redo list has no order, and it is empty. The v2 Most-missed strip ranks by hit count, which favours whatever the student happened to practise most.
proposals.needs:
- A TOPIC_SHARE constant in blueprint.py.
- The miss rate from attempts.
- estimate.py's slope for the optional points line (R16).
- sort=worth on GET /api/review/redo.

proposals.title: Your rulebook: write the rule when a mistake closes, and get it back on test eve
proposals.what:
When a mistake reaches Fixed, the pane and the session summary line ask, optionally: 'Write the rule in your own words'. The field takes 140 characters, with a placeholder drawn from the label (e.g. 'A whole circle is 360°, not 180°'). It is stored in traps.note (R9).
- The rule shows after the student answers each check-in ('Your rule: …'), and it stays editable.
- The Fixed tab gets a `List | Rulebook` toggle. Rulebook lists the rules grouped by habit or topic, each with one fresh mini example.
- **Print my rulebook** uses print CSS.
- Today's test-day checklist (the last 7 days) links 'Read your rulebook: 18 rules, about 6 min'.

What the student does differently: they write one line for each mistake they fix, and reread their own 20-odd rules the night before the test. Why it moves the score: the generation effect means explanations a student produces are remembered better than ones they read. A short personal list is the most useful final review there is, and no generic cheat sheet can match it.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's notes live only on exam highlights, and their Saved Content card is three counts. The v2 spec puts notes only on saved questions.
proposals.needs:
- traps.note (R9, already planned).
- The notes store (R6) for saved questions.
- print.html reuse (S10).
- The Today test-day checklist link (S3).

proposals.title: Burn-down and forecast: watch the backlog shrink toward the exam date
proposals.what:
The Fixed tab head gets a 12-week chart: for each week, a pair of bars (opened vs fixed) and a line for the open count. Beside it:
- a forecast: 'At your pace (8 fixed a week, 5 opened), open mistakes reach 0 on Oct 30, 8 days before your SAT.' Or: 'That lands after your SAT. 5 more minutes a day clears them by Nov 7.'
- the relapse rate, `3 of 40 relapsed (8%)`, and the median days to fix.

On Mondays, Today shows a recap line: 'Last week: 9 fixed, 2 relapsed, 5 new.' Me's Saved content card shows the open-count sparkline.

What the student does differently: they see their net progress, and get a concrete minutes-per-day target tied to their exam date. Why it moves the score: visible progress toward a dated goal keeps students practising. Tying the backlog to the exam turns a vague list into a plan, and the student can see it working.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep never shows what was fixed; Profile's 'Redo Questions 0' is the whole story. The v2 spec has a one-line stat.
proposals.needs:
- SQL over traps.opened and traps.closed by X-Tz week.
- learners.exam_date and minutes (R15).
- A chart in the dataviz tokens (F1).
- The Today recap line (S3).

proposals.title: Grade a paper worksheet in 30 seconds, so offline work counts
proposals.what:
The printable worksheet (§16) carries a short code and a QR on each page. Its answer page, `/review/print/?w=CODE`, has one row per number: A–D buttons, or a grid-in field with the usual keystroke filter, plus an optional 'minutes spent' box.

Submitting files each answer through progress.record with source 'worksheet'. The seeds are fresh and unseen, so right answers are clean. ms is the total divided by n. Mistakes are named and opened, and pips fill, exactly as online. The worksheet footer says 'Grade it at …/w/CODE' instead of 'These answers are not filed'.

What the student does differently: they do a worksheet on the bus or in study hall and get the same named-mistake feedback and credit as online. Why it moves the score: more retrieval practice without a screen, and none of it is lost. Today the spec's worksheet uses up seeds and files nothing, so a miss on paper never reaches Redo.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has no printable practice at all. The v2 worksheet says 'These answers are not filed'.
proposals.needs:
- sets (R18) with kind 'worksheet', or a worksheets(code, learner, items, at) table.
- POST /api/review/worksheet/{code}/grade, owner only, once per code.
- Source 'worksheet' already exists in §2.6.

parity_gaps.feature: Redo all / Fix all as a one-sitting backlog
parity_gaps.spec_says: `Redo all · 22 questions` queues each template max(owed) times in one set, all templates once before a second round. The repair right after a miss counts as a clean answer.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is TopTierPrep's 'Redo Only' filter, made to work: a list worked through in one sitting. A trap can close within minutes of opening, on recognition of the label just read.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Today's queue (proposal 1) plus closing on two different days (proposal 2): one answer per template per day, mixed with cover questions, so 'Fixed' means the student recalled it after a delay.

parity_gaps.feature: Marked tab and Mark for review (flags)
parity_gaps.spec_says: A flag per sitting. The Marked tab is grouped by sitting with pick → key and time. The calibration line reads 'You flagged 12 · 7 were right (58%)'.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is TopTierPrep's Mark for Review / FOR REVIEW / Flagged (n), kept after the session, plus one ratio. Nothing says what a flag was for, or whether going back paid off.
parity_gaps.upgrade:
- A one-tap flag reason in both runners (Between two · Too long · Guessing · Check later), stored in flags.why, and Marked grouped by reason.
- A 'flag lab' across sittings from qstate.first and changes: flags returned to, answers changed wrong→right vs right→wrong, the net gain per flag, and a rule per topic.
- Flagged items go into Today's review.
- The confidence grid of proposal 4 replaces the single ratio.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Rows with a 280-character note; Again, exactly / Fresh versions / Share / Print / Unsave; pages of 50.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is TopTierPrep's 'Saved Only' pool with a list view. A bookmark drawer that never comes back to the student is forgotten, and their own vocab 'Due Today' already beats it for words.
parity_gaps.upgrade:
- Saved becomes a spaced deck on fresh numbers (ladder 1/3/7/21/60 days, proposal 1), with `Saved · 3 due` on the tab.
- The note shows as 'Your hint' after the student answers.
- A one-tap reason at save time (Nice trick · Hard · Got lucky · Ask a tutor): 'Got lucky' opens an Unsure mistake, and 'Ask a tutor' drafts a help share.

parity_gaps.spec_says: A table of every try on the whole template (date, source, difficulty, result, misconception, time, flag), with summary counts and Open.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Wider in scope, but still TopTierPrep's row log ('#1 ⊗ Incorrect · Option A · 00:22'). The student has to read the rows to work out whether they are improving.
parity_gaps.upgrade:
- A header chart of the question type's tries: result cells over time, a time line and the pace target.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Hide answers hides the key, the option lines and the rationale, stays on across Next, and 'Check' re-answers the exact item, filed as a Repeat.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Up to 5 chips ordered by ×hits, then 'Redo these 5'.
